steps.title: Prepare the view
steps.body: The sidebar shrinks to icons and the integrated terminal opens below the dashboard. The Debian session represents the device requesting its identity.

steps.title: Example DMS
steps.body: EST Showcase identifies the registration authority and contains the policy applied to requests.

steps.title: Automatic registration
steps.body: Just-in-time provisioning creates a record for an unknown identifier at enrollment. The CSR CN is the identifier in this example.

steps.title: EST protocol
steps.body: EST RFC 7030 provides the simpleenroll operation for certificate requests. The displayed CA and profile determine issuance.

steps.title: Initial authentication
steps.body: Both initial authentication methods are disabled in this synthetic environment. Any client that can reach it can request a certificate.
steps.note: NO_AUTH over HTTP is only for this isolated demonstration; the project quickstart uses HTTPS and a bootstrap certificate.

steps.title: Check the CSR
steps.body: Verify CSR signature controls whether the request signature is validated. It is changed temporarily to show the setting.

steps.title: Enable verification
steps.body: The switch is enabled again before saving. An invalid signature should cause the request to be rejected.

steps.title: Save policy
steps.body: Save changes applies the DMS configuration to future requests. JITP, EST and signature verification remain enabled in the recording.

steps.title: Key and CSR
steps.body: An EC P-256 key is generated in a temporary client directory, a CSR is created with CN sensor-demo-930, and it is encoded as DER and Base64 for EST. The private key is never printed.

steps.title: EST endpoint
steps.body: The path includes the DMS ID est-showcase. The address 172.17.0.1 is specific to the Docker host used for this recording.

steps.title: Simpleenroll request
steps.body: curl sends the CSR with Content-Type application/pkcs10 and saves the response in enroll.b64. This laboratory DMS does not require initial credentials.

steps.title: Server response
steps.body: HTTP 200 shows that the request completed successfully. The response contains a Base64-encoded certificate package.

steps.title: Inspect the certificate
steps.body: OpenSSL extracts the certificate from the PKCS#7 response and displays its subject, issuer and serial number. The private key remains on the client.

steps.title: Issued identity
steps.body: The subject contains the requested CN and the issuer is Acme Device CA. Note the serial number to compare it with the dashboard.

steps.title: Device inventory
steps.body: The Devices view lets you find the record created by JITP during issuance.

steps.title: Search by CN
steps.body: The filter uses the same identifier that appears in the CSR and certificate subject.

steps.title: Open the device
steps.body: The detail view shows the newly created record and its associated identity.

steps.title: Registration authority
steps.body: The device detail shows its owning DMS. It should be EST Showcase.

steps.title: Associated certificate
steps.body: View certificate opens the certificate linked to the device identity.

steps.title: Compare the serial
steps.body: The dashboard and OpenSSL output show the same serial value; the interface adds separators and changes letter casing.
